title: AMD, QCOM Targets Raised While INTC, COHR Face Cuts — Susquehanna Sees ‘Modest Upside’ For Chip Earnings
detail:
AMD, QCOM Targets Raised While INTC, COHR Face Cuts — Susquehanna Sees ‘Modest Upside’ For Chip Earnings
Harshita Tyagi
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 7:30 AM MST 4 min read
INTC
AMD
QCOM
COHR
ON
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Susquehanna expects "modest upside" to third-quarter semiconductor earnings and fourth-quarter guidance, citing AI demand and a continuing broader industry upcycle.

The firm raised its AMD price target to $620 from $550 and Qualcomm to $185 from $160, maintaining its ratings.

Susquehanna cut targets on Coherent and Onsemi, but maintained 'Positive' ratings on both.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) saw their price targets raised by Susquehanna on Wednesday, while Intel Corp. (INTC) and Coherent Corp. (COHR) faced cuts as the firm revised its outlook for semiconductor stocks ahead of quarterly earnings.

Susquehanna expects "modest upside" to third-quarter earnings and fourth-quarter guidance, driven largely by artificial intelligence (AI) demand, while the broader semiconductor upcycle continues, according to The Fly.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

At the time of this writing, QCOM and AMD stocks were trading nearly 1% higher, while COHR was up more than 1%. Meanwhile, INTC shares were in the red.

AMD, QCOM And SKWS See Higher Targets

Susquehanna raised AMD's price target to $620 from $550, maintaining a 'Positive' rating. It also raised QCOM's target to $185 from $160 and Skyworks Solutions' (SWKS) target to $90 from $65, maintaining 'Neutral' ratings on both.

The revisions come as AMD expects third-quarter revenue of approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, representing roughly 41% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. AMD's second-quarter revenue rose 50% to $11.5 billion, including a 107% jump in data-center revenue to $6.7 billion, driven by demand for EPYC processors and Instinct graphics processing units.

Qualcomm, meanwhile, reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $9.9 billion in July and expects non-handset revenue growth, including data centers, to exceed 60% in fiscal 2027, compared with 24% in fiscal 2026.

COHR, INTC And ON Face Target Cuts

Susquehanna cut its price targets by 20% for ON stock, about 18% for COHR stock, 17% for WOLF and 9% for INTC. The firm maintained 'Positive' ratings on Onsemi and Coherent and 'Neutral' ratings on Wolfspeed and Intel, according to The Fly.

Coherent, which supplies optical technologies used in AI infrastructure, reported fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) revenue of $2.05 billion and forecast fiscal first-quarter (Q1) 2027 revenue of $2.2 billion to $2.4 billion.

Intel, meanwhile, forecast third-quarter revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion after reporting 25% year-over-year growth in second-quarter sales.

title: Intel Stock Still Trades at 84 Times Earnings After a 35% Drop. I'm Not Buying Yet.
detail:
Intel Stock Still Trades at 84 Times Earnings After a 35% Drop. I'm Not Buying Yet.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:01 AM MST 5 min read
INTC
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Analysts with JPMorgan Chase upgraded Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) to neutral from underweight on Monday, Oct. 19, citing growing agentic artificial intelligence (AI) workloads and tight supplies of advanced chips. The chipmaker's stock gained around 2% that day, ending at $92.03.

Even after that bounce, shares are around 35% under their record close of $140.94 on June 22. And most of the drop has happened lately. The stock still closed above $127 as late as Sept. 24.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Sure, an upgrade to neutral isn't a call to buy, and I wouldn't buy or sell a stock based on an analyst's rating anyway. What matters more is how much investors now pay for what Intel earns. And by that measure, the stock has gotten far cheaper than its 35% drop suggests.

Image source: Intel.

Intel's earnings have nearly doubled

When Intel set its record in June, its four most recently reported quarters came to non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share of just $0.57. That figure included a loss of $0.10 a share in the second quarter of 2025.

At $140.94, then, investors were paying almost 250 times Intel's adjusted earnings for the previous four quarters.

Intel's second-quarter results, released in July, changed that. Revenue rose 25% year over year to $16.1 billion, accelerating sharply from 7% growth in the first quarter and a 4% fall in the fourth quarter of 2025. And adjusted earnings per share climbed to $0.42, up from $0.15 in the fourth quarter of 2025 and $0.29 in the first quarter of 2026.

Combined, the past four reported quarters now total $1.09 a share in adjusted earnings -- nearly double the June number.

At around $92 as I write, Intel trades at about 84 times these earnings. It's still a steep price-to-earnings ratio. But it's around a third of where the ratio was at the record, even though the share price fell only about 35%. In other words, rising profits did more to cut the stock's price-to-earnings ratio than the falling share price did.

Intel's GAAP results look much worse. On that basis, the company lost $2.16 a share for the second quarter. But a non-cash charge of $2.45 a share more than accounted for the loss. The charge is linked to Intel stock held in escrow for the U.S. government under its CHIPS Act deal, so I'm leaning on the adjusted numbers here.

title: Apple vs. Intel: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Apple vs. Intel: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Erin Kennedy, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:20 AM MST 5 min read
AAPL
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Should you stick with a proven cash-flow machine or bet on a classic tech turnaround story? Today we're comparing Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) to determine which is the better buy.

Apple dominates the high-end consumer market with its ecosystem of devices, while Intel is reinventing itself through its foundry operations. These tech giants represent two distinct strategies for growth, making a side-by-side comparison essential for investors navigating the current market.

The case for Apple

Apple designs and manufactures mobile communication devices and personal computers for a global audience, distributing its products to consumers and enterprise clients across more than 200 countries. It uses a mix of direct sales through 201 retail stores and indirect channels like cellular network carriers and third-party resellers. The company also licenses its platforms to search service providers and relies on a global network of third-party software developers for its app ecosystem.

In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $416.2 billion, reflecting a growth rate of approximately 6.4% over the prior year. This increase supported net income of close to $112 billion, up from $93.7 billion in 2024. Net margin was roughly 26.9%, showing the company's ability to maintain high profitability despite shifting consumer spending patterns.

As of Apple's September 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is nearly 1.5. This metric compares total debt to shareholders' equity, indicating how much leverage the business uses to fund its operations. The current ratio is roughly 0.9, while free cash flow reached close to $98.8 billion for the period, which supports research and development and shareholder returns.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures a wide range of processors and accelerators for the data center and edge computing markets. Its Intel Foundry business is a major strategic focus, offering manufacturing and packaging services to other semiconductor stocks. The company employs over 108,000 people to support its mission of providing domestic manufacturing capacity for the global technology industry.

In fiscal 2025, revenue reached roughly $52.9 billion, a minor decline of about 0.5%. The company recorded a net loss of nearly $267 million, a substantial improvement over the $18.8 billion net loss reported in the prior year. This trend suggests the business is beginning to stabilize even as it continues its expensive transition toward a new manufacturing model.
